The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T03:36:05Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T03:36:30Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-11T03:30:00Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T03:41:10Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 11 minutes 10 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 4 minutes 44 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T03:41:10Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 33.5% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 40.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 32.5% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 1% {series_before} before it began, 33.54166666666667% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 40.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 8,025.67 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of monthly-spend-feature, each in its own words:
      C1: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-11T03:29:57Z {C1.1}. Account page requests then began failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% {C1.2} to about 34% {C1.3}. No deployment was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, refuted]
      C2: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 2026-11-11T03:29:57Z {C1.5}. This sent account page requests through src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, where line 47 {C1.6} raises ZeroDivisionError. The error rate stepped from about 1% {C1.7} to about 35% {C1.8} at 2026-11-11T03:30:00Z {C1.9}. No code or configuration deployed, and latency, memory and CPU stayed flat. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.88 {C1.10}, refuted, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py builds the list of purchases with `in_current_month` set, then divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by the length of that list. Its divisor is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not yet this month. That is a normal state for a real account, and it covers nearly every account early in a month. `render_spend_summary` calls this function whenever `use_monthly_summary` is set and `use_typical_spend` is not. So switching on monthly-spend-feature sent those shoppers' requests to a `//` with a zero divisor, and the broad handler in `serve_account_page` (src/io_shop/account_page.py) turned the ZeroDivisionError into a failed page.
      
      The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0 {F1.1}, which is the average spend per item over an empty month. Otherwise it divides exactly as before. The page then renders a figure for these shoppers whether the flag is on or off. Nothing is swallowed: the lifetime average (`average_spend_per_item`) is unchanged and still raises for an account with no purchases at all. The existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py assert that it raises and that the failure names a `//` line in spend_summary.py, and that path is untouched.
      
      The tests: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gets two new cases using the existing `an_account_with_no_purchases_this_month` helper. One checks that the monthly average is 0 {F1.2}. The other checks that `render_spend_summary` with `use_monthly_summary=True` returns 0 {F1.3}. Against the current code both cases would raise ZeroDivisionError.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #548 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month. The divisor is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not yet this month, so the account page request raises ZeroDivisionError. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending feature, and it sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, likely for shoppers who had not bought anything yet this month, so those pages failed to load.
still_at_risk: Account page requests could keep failing with a division by zero for as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed
stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again in a way that reaches io-shop. Confirm at the service that its flag evaluation log lines read monthly-spend-feature=off and that ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is no longer logged for account page requests.
why_it_did_not_help: Find out why io-shop kept logging monthly-spend-feature=on evaluations after the flag was switched off at {P2.1}: whether the change reached the service's flag evaluation at all, and if so through what cache or refresh. If it did reach the service, find out why account pages still failed.
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged account page error rates far above their usual level. (cites Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The account page requests failed because building the page raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The service logged this error during {G5309.3} and not before. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: Requests reached that code because admin switched feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The service evaluated the flag as off during {G7e5d.4}, partly on in {G971b.6}, and on for every evaluation during {Gce95.4}. The division errors began in the first minute the flag was on for every evaluation. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: Shoppers closing their connections, the account page error logged before the onset: it was logged only during {G46bc.3}, while account pages were rendering normally. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: Switching the flag on broke the page because, as Code-Fix read the source, the flag sends account pages through a monthly average per item whose divisor is zero for shoppers who have bought nothing yet this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: No test or check was seen that ran the code path monthly-spend-feature turns on against an account with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says the existing tests do not cover that case.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag reached production shoppers.
contributing_factors 2: The flag went from a few evaluations on to every evaluation on in the next minute. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of account page requests would have failed, and the rollout could have stopped before it reached all shoppers.
contributing_factors 3: As Code-Fix read the source, a broad handler in serve_account_page turns any exception in the spend summary into a failed account page rather than leaving that section out.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: Shoppers would still have got their account page, just without the spend summary, even with the division by zero still in place.
contributing_factors 4: No on-call person was paged when the HighErrorRate alert fired on io-shop.
contributing_factors 4 had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have known of the failing pages and could have stepped in when the automated revert did not end the errors, which may have shortened the incident.
action_items 1: Require that the code path a feature flag turns on in io-shop is covered by tests before that flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 2: Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, then widen in stages.
action_items 3: Halt a staged flag rollout automatically, and switch the flag back, when the service's error rate rises above its baseline.
action_items 4: Make serve_account_page render the account page without the spend summary when the summary fails, instead of failing the whole page.
action_items 5: Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call person.
went_wrong 1: The Mitigation Agent judged the revert refuted while io-shop's own flag evaluations still logged monthly-spend-feature=on in {Gce95.5}, after the flag had been switched off.
went_wrong 2: Argus found an earlier incident in memory, 9c1d4e7a-0000-4000-8000-00000000fee1, where reverting this same flag had been refuted, and tried the same revert again without first finding out why it had not helped then.
went_wrong 3: The second investigation formed only C2, which blamed the same flag change that had already been tried, so it gave Argus nothing new to try.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
